boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in the Goldsboro Expedition. Preserve per-engagement dates: Kinston December 14, White Hall December 16 and Goldsborough Bridge December 17, 1862. Skirmishes on other days (Southwest Creek, Mount Olive, Thompson's Bridge) are not added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names Amory's and Stevenson's Brigades against Robertson's Brigade; the live field reads zero. Foster says the Ninth New Jersey and Amory's brigade were posted on the bank with several batteries; his cavalry on December 15 found one Confederate regiment and four guns at the bridge.
claims.rationale: Formation descriptions only; the December 15 sighting precedes the interval. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The commanders' reports each claim success; neither is adopted, and the frozen label is retained.

open_questions: Robertson's report, returns and casualty allocation for White Hall remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Foster's reports and G. W. Smith's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XVIII, are two further families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
